title: Bullwhip Effect
equation: Upstream Swing = Demand Swing × Tiers Amplified
hook: Customers bought a little more this week, and suddenly your supplier thinks it's a boom.
statement: Small changes in customer demand turn into huge swings the further back up the supply chain you go.
explainer: Each link over-orders to protect itself, so a tiny bump at the register becomes a giant surge at the factory. Know the real signal before you react to the noise.
sop: Measure how much real customer demand moves week to week.
Count the tiers between your customer and your furthest supplier.
Multiply Demand Swing by Tiers Amplified to see the upstream hit.
Share real sales data with your suppliers.
Use steady reorder rules so you're not adding to the swing.
equation_example: Customer demand moves 10%, with 4 tiers between the customer and the raw material supplier. 10% × 4 = a 40% swing at the top. More tiers and less shared data make it worse. A short, open chain keeps it small.
question: Compare last month's orders to suppliers against your actual customer sales. Note the gap.
closing_statement: Find the real signal before you amplify it.
